players.note: Nakobe Dean was back at it in Week 9, racking up seven solos, 11 assists, and one tackle for loss. Dean has been an elite option all season and should continue to be treated as a top-five play for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Arvell Reese went off in Week 9, exploding with 10 solos, two assists, three sacks, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Reese proved he can have an early-career Micah Parsons like impact, logging three sacks, with just one coming off the edge. Reese is up to 4.5 sacks on the season and has pushed his way to LB1 in fppg after nine weeks of action. Count Reese as a top-five play at the position going forward.

Fred Warner was excellent in Week 9, racking up three solos, two assists, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Warner remains locked in as a top-10 option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Carson Schwesinger went off in Week 9, exploding with 10 solos, five assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Carson re-established himself as one of the elite options at the position with this performance and should once again be considered a top-five option. The LB7 in fppg, fire Schwesinger up with confidence for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Houston Texans.

Jacob Rodriguez was excellent in Week 9, tallying seven solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Rodriguez already has three splash weeks to his name, checking into Week 10 as the LB12 in fppg. Fire the rookie linebacker up as a top-10 option for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Jordyn Brooks was back at it in Week 9, racking up four solos, eight assists, and one tackle for loss. Brooks has caught fire with three straight spike weeks and is once again locked in as a top-12 play. Treat him as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Micah McFadden was back at it in Week 9, tallying five solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. McFadden has made waves by recording back-to-back spike weeks since stepping in as starter for the injured Tremaine Edmunds, forcing his way into the top-25 conversation. Count him as just that for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Washington Commanders.

Nick Bolton was excellent in Week 9, racking up five solos, seven assists, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Bolton is back in LB1 form and should be treated as just that for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Isaiah McDuffie was excellent in Week 9, reeling off five solos, five assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. McDuffie now has a splash week and spike week in his last three games, and should have at least one more game with starter snaps, with Zaire Franklin expected to be sidelined for at least one more week. McDuffie has recorded five or more solos in three of his last four and should be counted as a top-25 option until Franklin returns, at which point he will revert back to more of a top-36 play.

Barrett Carter showed up in Week 9, racking up two solos, eight assists, one forced fumble, one interception, and one pass defended. The LB13 in fppg, Carter can be counted as a weekly top-15 option, including this week against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Sonny Styles was back at it in Week 9, tallying six solos, seven assists, and one tackle for loss. Styles has five spike weeks on the season, with three of them coming in his last four games. Now the LB19 in fppg, Styles is safe to count as a top-25 option for a plus Week 10 matchup against the New York Giants on Thursday Night Football.

Devin Lloyd was back at it in Week 9, racking up five solos, three assists, and one pass defended. Lloyd had two straight duds, so a return back to his LB1 form is a welcome sight. Tap the Panthers linebacker as a top-12 play where needed.

Foyesade Oluokun was at it again in Week 9, tallying six solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Oluokun is a strong LB1 option for Week 10 and beyond and should be treated as such for a plus matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Frankie Luvu showed out in Week 9, racking up seven solos, eight assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. It was the first splash week of the season for Luvu, who has been solid but has lacked a signature performance until this past weekend. Luvu can be counted as a top-25 option during the heavy byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the New York Giants.

Dre Greenlaw was back at it in Week 9, tallying five solos, three assists, three tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery. Greenlaw has been one of the hotter linebackers in the league, but with an ejection, a suspension, and a bye, his production has flown a bit under the radar. Tap Greenlaw as a top-25 option for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

CJ Allen was at it again in Week 9, racking up three solos, seven assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Allen has put together back-to-back spike weeks since stepping in as the new MIKE for the Colts and appears poised to break into the top-15 conversation before long. For now, continue to treat him as a top-20 play for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Drue Tranquill was excellent in Week 9, tallying seven solos and six assists. Drue has four spike weeks to his name and should continue to be counted as a borderline top-25 play. Treat him as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Demario Davis was excellent in Week 9, racking up five solos, four assists, and one fumble recovery. Demario has found himself back in the LB2 conversation this season thanks to his consistent production. Treat him as a top-25 option for a plus matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Patrick Queen was back at it in Week 8, tallying three solos, nine assists, 1.5 sacks, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Queen had been quiet prior to Week 7, but now has back-to-back splash weeks under his belt, making him an LB2 consideration for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. Start him everywhere while he's cooking.

Tyrel Dodson got the start with Bobby Okereke sidelined and responded with seven solos and one assist. Dodson has been a valuable IDP contributor in the past, but his issues in coverage have pushed him off the field. Dodson will be a solid LB3 option if Okereke misses Week 10. This is a situation to monitor.

Terrel Bernard stepped up in Week 9, reeling off two solos, four assists, one interception, and two passes defended. Bernard has been a solid LB3 option and should continue to be treated as one for a plus Week 10 matchup against the New York Jets.

Andrew Van Ginkel was at it again in Week 9, racking up two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. AVG is up to 7.5 sacks on the season, with 3.5 of them coming in his last two games. The DL10 in fppg, Van Ginkel is a top-15 play whenever he is in the midst of a hot streak. Count him as just that for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

David Bailey stayed hot in Week 9, racking up five solos, four assists, two sacks, three tackles for loss, and two forced fumbles. The DL1 overall and in fppg, Bailey is up to 7.5 sacks on the season. Count the Jets edge rusher as a top-five play for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

T.J. Watt was back at it in Week 8, reeling off two solos, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. T.J. is up to 7.5 sacks on the season, with three of them coming in his last two games. The DL5 in fppg heading into the Steelers' Week 9 bye, treat Watt as an easy top-five option for a tasty Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Myles Garrett returned with a bang in Week 9, racking up three solos, three sacks, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Garrett delivered and then overdelivered in his first game as a Ram and is obviously locked back in as a top-five option going forward.

Carl Granderson stayed hot in Week 9, tallying five solos, two assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Granderson has been on fire for the Saints and is now up to 7.5 sacks on the season, with at least 1.5 sacks in an incredible four straight games. Granderson needs to be treated as a top-15 play until he cools down. Act accordingly ahead of a plus Week 10 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Greg Rousseau was back at it in Week 9, reeling off one solo, one sack, one tackle for loss, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended. The Bills edge rusher is up to eight sacks on the season, with a sack in each of his last two games. Fire Rousseau up as a top-10 option for a tasty Week 10 matchup against the New York Jets.

Dallas Turner was excellent in Week 9, racking up two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Ninth in the league with 7.0 sacks, Turner is locked in as a top-12 DL option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Bryce Boettcher got the start in Week 9 and responded with four solos and eight assists. Boettcher filled in for Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) and could get another start if ADG is forced to miss any more time. Treat the Colts linebacker as a Lb4/flex2 type for as long as he is getting starts.

Rashan Gary was excellent in Week 9, racking up five solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Rashan has just two sacks on the season, but still makes for a DL3/4 type at best. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 10 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Jacob Martin went berserk in Week 8, tallying four solos, three sacks, and three tackles for loss. Martin clawed his way up to 6.5 sacks in seven games, with five of them coming in three of his last four games. Appearing in this column for the second straight week despite just coming off a bye, Martin's rostership numbers didn't move an inch, theoretically because IDP managers didn't want to burn a spot on him just to have him go on bye. Whatever the case, Martin needs to be treated as a DL2 option while he is hot and may find a new home by the end of the day (Tuesday). Tap Martin as a top-25 option until he starts to cool down.

DeMarcus Lawrence stepped up in Week 9, posting two solos, one assist, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. It was the first sack of the season for the Seahawks edge rusher, who saw a season high in snaps (74%) with Leonard Williams sidelined. Continue to treat Lawrence as a low floor DL3/4, regardless of whether or not Williams returns for Week 10.

Patrick Jones stepped up in Week 9, notching four solos, two assists, one sack, and three tackles for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Jones, who remains more DL5 than DL4 until Week 11 when six teams are on bye. Look elsewhere for Week 10.

DJ Wonnum is expected to clear concussion protocol in time to suit up for Week 10. If he flies to Munich, he should be considered a lock for the Sunday morning matchup against the New England Patriots. Tap Wonnum as a DL3 option if he is active, as expected.

Josh Uche was back at it in Week 9, recording four solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Uche has just three sacks on the season, but with a sack in back-to-back games, he is now an intriguing DL3 option, especially during the byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 10 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Clowney is set to get the start for Week 10 with Danielle Hunter ruled out. Up to 3.5 sacks on the season after getting to the quarterback last week, Jadeveon can be counted as a top-36 option for the plus Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Caden Curry was back at it in Week 9, reeling off one solo, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. Curry has back-to-back spike weeks and has found himself joining the DL3 conversation. Fire the Colts edge rusher up as an upside DL3 option for a tasty Week 10 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.
